subject: Materials Science
title: Chemical Attack on Polymers
description: A quick, practical guide to Chemical Attack on Polymers.

hook.text: A rubber gasket swells when it contacts gasoline — the fuel dissolves into the polymer and weakens it.

buildup.text: Solvents can swell, dissolve, or crack polymers — compatibility depends on matching chemical polarity.

discovery.text: 'Like dissolves like' — polar solvents attack polar polymers. Nylon resists oil but absorbs water.

twist.text: Environmental stress cracking combines chemical exposure with mechanical stress — failure at lower levels of either.

climax.text: Chemical resistance charts guide engineers in choosing the right polymer for each fluid — every combination differs.

punchline.text: The wrong chemical turns a strong polymer into a soft sponge.

quiz.question: What principle governs solvent attack on polymers?
options: Like dissolves like — matching polarity determines susceptibility
